articles.title_orig: China, Turkey and Ethiopia Launch Initiative To Strengthen Global Carbon Credit Markets
articles.title_zh: China, Turkey and Ethiopia Launch Initiative To Strengthen Global Carbon Credit Markets
articles.content_orig:
China, Turkey and Ethiopia launched a joint initiative Wednesday at the COP31 United Nations climate conference to improve international carbon credit trading, increase the availability of reliable credits and strengthen cooperation between participating countries.
The agreement, announced at a high-level gathering in the China Pavilion, proposes a framework for governments and market participants to coordinate policies, exchange information and develop carbon trading systems.
Turkey is hosting COP31, while Ethiopia will host COP32.
Under the initiative, governments and intergovernmental organizations are encouraged to establish stronger oversight of carbon credit programs and improve standards governing the credits issued. The proposal also seeks closer cooperation among trading systems and greater participation in projects that generate carbon credits.

Participation is voluntary, and the arrangement carries no legal obligations. Countries joining the initiative will not be required to recognize one another’s carbon credits, connect their trading platforms or registries, exchange data or provide funding.
Nor does the agreement automatically permit international transfers of carbon credits under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, which establishes rules for international cooperation through carbon markets.
Beyond improving trading standards, the initiative provides for joint projects, technical assistance and policy discussions. It encourages responsible credit purchases and cooperation on the infrastructure needed to support carbon markets.
Li said these measures could help carbon credits contribute more effectively to international climate efforts and the transition toward lower-carbon economies.
COP31, formally the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, opened Monday and continues through Nov. 20.

articles.title_orig: Megaspeed's vacant offices raise questions about ties to Nvidia and China
articles.title_zh: Megaspeed's vacant offices raise questions about ties to Nvidia and China
articles.content_orig:
The unusual global footprint of Megaspeed International, the Singapore-based company at the center of the Nvidia Chinese spy scandal, is fueling questions about whether it's a front for the Chinese government.
One of Megaspeed's leaders is Alice Huang, the woman with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was having an affair, and who is suspected by U.S. intelligence of being an asset of China's Ministry of State Security . In the past three years, Megaspeed, formerly a gaming company, has been one of Nvidia's biggest foreign customers, purchasing nearly $5 billion in AI chips and advanced hardware, The New York Times first reported.
And yet Megaspeed's corporate headquarters sat practically empty, according to The Straits Times, an English-language newspaper in Singapore. Questions have also been raised about its outposts in Australia and Malaysia.
Published reports in recent days revealed that the company listed a newspaper vendor as the director of its Australian subsidiary, and one of its Malaysia offices consisted of a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur. Yet another Malaysia office was tucked into a shopping mall.
Megaspeed began as an offshoot of a China-based gaming firm and grew into a juggernaut by gaining access to restricted Nvidia AI computer chips. U.S. investigators say that Alice Huang used her contacts in the industry and a series of shell companies to gain access to 240,000 chips banned for export into China. Now it is being probed in both the U.S. and Singapore for allegedly smuggling those chips into China.
In a statement Thursday, Megaspeed said it "takes its compliance obligations under U.S. export control laws extremely seriously" and that it's "committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government."
President Trump said this week the FBI is also investigating romantic and business ties between Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang and Alice Huang (who are not related).
Earlier this week, Jensen Huang, who is married, apologized for the affair in a statement to Nvidia's employees. The company launched an independent investigation of the matter , and an Nvidia shareholder filed a class action lawsuit Tuesday alleging that Huang concealed a relationship with Alice Huang and misled shareholders about national security concerns raised by the relationship.
Nvidia's board said Sunday that it had no reason to believe that the company's secrets or national security were compromised. "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," its statement said.
However, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News on Wednesday that the board was preparing to oust Jensen Huang, a development that was first reported by the Wall Street Journal.
China expert Jacqueline Deal said that Nvidia's advanced AI chips could have ended up with the Chinese military. Deal, who is an adviser to State Armor, a nonprofit that studies global security threats, told CBS News, "If allegations are true, who will be fired? Nvidia has a compliance team that may have failed utterly."
She also questioned the effectiveness of the U.S. Commerce Department, which has jurisdiction over export controls that may have been bypassed, potentially giving the Chinese military access to the world's most advanced chips.
Here's what we now know about Megaspeed:
It is a major Nvidia customer. Megaspeed and its Malaysian affiliate, Speedmatrix, purchased $4.8 billion of Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence equipment and processors over the last three years.
In 2025, Megaspeed International faced an investigation by Singapore police for alleged breaches of local laws, but no details have emerged about the probe, according to The Straits Times.
"Megaspeed International is a premier business partner of NVIDIA, strategically positioned in the Asia Pacific region," according to its LinkedIn profile, which claims it has between 201 and 500 employees. Three years ago it listed between two and 10 employees, according to the South China Morning Post.
Megaspeed International did not reply to a request for comment. It posted an "official statement" on its website addressing what it called "misleading information" and "incorrect insinuations" accusing it of involvement in illegal chip transfers.
"We want to be absolutely clear over the past six months our company has undergone multiple on-site inspections and reviews by key institutions, including the Bureau of Industry and Security of the US Commerce Department, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry of Malaysia and NVIDIA," said the message, which also appeared on the company's LinkedIn page.
"These thorough investigations have confirmed that there has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities," the company said.
But in a statement on Thursday, the company said it had "retained a leading U.S. law firm to ... independently verify its export control compliance practices. Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws."
Megaspeed was originally incorporated in 2015 under the name 7Road International, a subsidiary of a Chinese developer of popular video games and mobile apps based in Shenzhen, China, according to corporate filings.
Huang Le Limited, a shell company in the British Virgin Islands, acquired 7Road International in March 2023. Huang Le is the Chinese name of Alice Huang.
That same month, 7Road International was renamed Megaspeed International, and Huang became its managing director. The company also launched a subsidiary called Speedmatrix.
By the end of October 2023, Huang and another Megaspeed director, Cang Yang, resigned from the company after it was bought up by a firm called Swiftdata, whose director is based in China, documents show.
But there's some indication Huang may still be affiliated with the company. Culper Research, an activist short-selling firm , published a 40-page report on Nvidia in May that cited Megaspeed employees who said Huang was still running the company.
The report also raised some concern about Jensen Huang's relationship with Megaspeed and Alice Huang, stating, "Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has not only vouched for Megaspeed, but seems to have quite literally walked alongside Megaspeed at every step, while maintaining an uncomfortably close relationship with Megaspeed's Alice Huang, a Chinese national."
Megaspeed lists its headquarters office address on the seventh floor of the Ocean Financial Centre in Singapore, a glass office tower in Singapore's central business district.
When the Straits Times and The New York Times visited the Singapore offices around the same time late last year, they found little or no staff working. The Straits Times said the door was locked, and the Times found just two people in its office on a workday.
Megaspeed has an Australian subsidiary on the 10th floor of a commercial and retail tower in the heart of Sydney's central business district. Forty other businesses are on the same floor, and space in the building can be rented for as little as $17 per day, Australia's ABC News reported. Corporate filings name Shanghai-born Kai Kang, a 29-year-old newspaper vendor, as the director, according to Australian news reports. But Kang's newsstand is in Northern Victoria, over 400 miles from Sydney. Kang's father told Australia's ABC News this week that he had never heard of Megaspeed.

articles.title_orig: Mammoth crowds greet Pope Leo on return to Peru, his adopted homeland
articles.title_zh: Mammoth crowds greet Pope Leo on return to Peru, his adopted homeland
articles.content_orig:
Lee el artículo en español
Riding on horseback to visit the most isolated Andean areas of his community, distributing food amid the Covid-19 pandemic, or wearing rubber boots in the water and mud of floods: this is how many Peruvians remember the man who is now Pope Leo XIV.
Robert Prevost was in the trenches and alongside his people during Peru’s most difficult moments, and many of these memories were likely front of mind among the millions who gathered to welcome the pope on his visit to his adopted homeland on Wednesday.
Pope Leo arrived in Callao city, near Lima, to a hero’s welcome with spectators at the airport waving flags and cheering as he stepped out of his plane and waved to the crowd. He was received by high-ranking officials including President Keiko Fujimori and Foreign Minister Carlos Espá.
Later, a sea of supporters lined the streets to salute him as his motorcade drove him to the government palace in the capital. The Vatican says an estimated 3 million people turned out, the largest crowd of his papacy so far. Earlier this week, roughly 2.5 million attended a mass he held in Argentina.
In a speech in front of Fujimori and the country’s political leaders, Leo said his return to Peru holds a “very special meaning” for him.
“That is why I can tell you, with deep gratitude, that I am also returning to my homeland,” he said.
Referencing the time he spent in the country, Leo said he had been made to “feel like one of their own” with people welcoming him into their homes and sharing with him “some good ceviche,” a traditional Peruvian fish dish. He also credited the country with “forming me as a shepherd.”
The pope’s trip to Peru, which will include visits to Cusco and Chiclayo, is widely seen as a homecoming for a pontiff who knows the country in depth and is a Peruvian citizen. In fact, he will receive a new Peruvian ID card that will list Chiclayo as his address.
A young Prevost first arrived in the South American country as a missionary in 1985. The years that followed shaped his leadership style, which would later lead him to become the successor to the late Pope Francis.
“I think he was heroic in many ways; he risked becoming ill. We lost 11 priests and a bishop emeritus during that time,” Father José Del Rosario recalls of the most difficult days of the pandemic.
Padre Robert, as he is known in Spanish in Peru, traveled more than 700 kilometers (435 miles) from Chiclayo to the Diocese of Callao, a province bordering the capital, Lima, where he served as apostolic administrator.
“He came every two weeks in his little car; he came alone in a simple pickup truck,” explained Del Rosario, parish priest and rector of the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Mount Carmel of La Legua, who worked closely with the then-bishop.
Pope! Amigo! Peruvians remember the young American priest who became pope
Prevost distributed food and everything needed by a population that lived under lockdown for months, while also offering spiritual guidance during the crisis.
“He gave us a lot of hope and cared for our people, a man who was very close to the people … and also very humble,” Del Rosario added.
Peru recorded more than 219,000 deaths , according to Johns Hopkins University figures, and one of the highest coronavirus mortality rates in the world. In Lima, and especially in the regions, terrifying scenes unfolded outside hospitals, with sick people collapsing in the street due to the shortage of oxygen, one of the key tools for treating the virus.
In Chiclayo, Bishop Prevost launched a fundraising campaign to purchase an oxygen plant. Together with Caritas Chiclayo, the bishop appealed to authorities and sectors of civil society and managed to raise more than US$380,000 for not just one but two oxygen plants.
Janinna Sesa, former director of Caritas Chiclayo, worked with the bishop for eight years, including during the pandemic, the flooding caused by the coastal El Niño in 2017, and Cyclone Yaku in 2023.
“We were always on the front lines, especially during disasters like the coastal El Niño phenomenon. He was the person who put on his boots and waded into the water; he helped people. He was very approachable and very kind,” Sesa told CNN.
Before leaving for Rome in 2023, after the late Pope Francis appointed him prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops and president of the Pontifical Commission for Latin America, Bishop Prevost also led appeals for aid for the more than 10,000 people affected by flooding caused by Cyclone Yaku in the north of the country.
“I ask you to be generous; I ask you to open your hearts so that we can help one another and move forward, as we have done in other times of crisis,” Prevost said in a video while standing in the water in the district of Illimo, in the Lambayeque region.
Examine the power held by popes throughout history
The assistance and response led by Prevost in the face of the massive arrival of Venezuelan migrants in 2018 was comprehensive and had a different vision from that of the country’s other regions.
Peru received more than 1.6 million Venezuelans through November 2025, the second-highest number in the region after Colombia. More than 20,000 of them passed through Chiclayo, and more than 3,500 families settled in the region, according to figures from the Commission for Human Mobility and Human Trafficking of the Diocese of Chiclayo. Prevost also promoted this commission to assist migrants and combat human trafficking.
First American pope marks July 4 on migrant island with plea for ‘compassion and generosity’
“The migration flow descended upon us, with thousands of migrants out on the streets, sleeping there, and the parishes serving as shelters,” Sesa recalled.
Father Robert was concerned not only with providing food and collecting clothing, blankets, and medicine, but also with building the San Vicente de Paúl village, which took them in at Puerto Etén.
“His simplicity, the peace he conveys, that serenity Monsignor Prevost had when listening to people — I still see it in Pope Leo XIV…. He welcomed us with such warmth, with so much love,” Lisbeth Díaz, a Venezuelan resident of Chiclayo and member of the Commission for Human Mobility and Human Trafficking, told CNN.
Prevost prioritized regularizing their legal status so they could work and integrate into society.
Prevost created spaces for dialogue and encouraged many people to raise their voices to denounce abuses during the internal conflict the country experienced beginning in the 1980s and to openly discuss the social reality during the authoritarian regime of the late President Alberto Fujimori in the 1990s.
At the Augustinian mission in Trujillo, the current pontiff and his seminarians traveled through towns and parishes in Andean areas, staging dramatizations that reflected the violence faced by peasants to encourage conversations that would help heal the trauma and pain they had suffered.
Prevost also participated in collecting signatures for the creation of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC), which investigated the violence between 1980 and 2000 and human rights abuses, particularly in rural Peru. Trujillo and the parishes led by the current pontiff collected the largest number of signatures.
Leo XIV is a pope forged in Peru. The nearly two decades he spent in the land he adopted as his own profoundly shaped his ministry and set him on the path to the papacy. As a bishop, Prevost was a pastor close to his flock, and at the Vatican, one of his closest collaborators is the Reverend Edgard Rimaycuna, a native of Chiclayo.
His work in South America and his leadership of the Order of Saint Augustine caught the attention of Pope Francis, who first appointed him bishop of Chiclayo and later brought him to Rome, where he went on to hold one of the most important positions in the Vatican and also became a cardinal. This made him a candidate in the 2025 conclave.

articles.title_orig: Ondas Posts Record Q3 2026 Revenue of $167.5 Million on Strong Bookings and Backlog Growth; Raises Full-Year Outlook - Ondas inc.
articles.title_zh: Ondas Posts Record Q3 2026 Revenue of $167.5 Million on Strong Bookings and Backlog Growth; Raises Full-Year Outlook - Ondas inc.
articles.content_orig:
WEST PALM BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 12, 2026 / Ondas Inc. (NASDAQ:ONDS) ("Ondas" or the "Company"), a leading provider of advanced autonomous systems and next-generation defense and security technologies and services, reported record financial and operating results for the third quarter of 2026. Ondas generated revenue of $167.5 million in the third quarter, compared with $83.8 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $10.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The results represent approximately 100% sequential revenue growth and more than a sixteen-fold year-over-year increase.
"This quarter demonstrates the growing benefits of Ondas' integrated operating platform," said Eric Brock, Chairman and CEO of Ondas. "Our businesses are gaining access to larger customers, broader channels, and stronger production and field-support capabilities, allowing mission-ready technologies to move more quickly from evaluation into deployment. The next phase is about disciplined execution: delivering on customer commitments, integrating our capabilities, and converting demand to sustainable growth and improving profitability."
"Our differentiation increasingly comes from combining autonomous systems, mission software, AI, and critical components into solutions that can be deployed and supported across multiple domains. Ondas Sentinel strengthens our ability to pursue and execute complex U.S. defense programs, while Regna AI extends our sovereign AI capabilities and creates opportunities to serve customers beyond our own hardware platforms. Together, these initiatives expand our addressable market, strengthen our customer relationships, and increase the software, services, and repeat revenue potential of the Ondas platform.
"We expect a strong finish to 2026, with momentum accelerating in the fourth quarter as volume deliveries ramp across existing programs and we convert pipeline opportunities into customer programs. Our order book remains healthy, our pipeline continues to expand, and our ability to produce, deliver, and sustain solutions for customers continues to strengthen. We are investing to support visible customer demand and build the production, supply-chain, deployment, and sustainment infrastructure required to deliver at scale. Over the next twelve months and beyond, we expect this growth to support meaningful operating leverage and improved profitability, supporting continued investment in innovation, market expansion, and long-term shareholder value."
Select Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Financial, Corporate and Business Development Highlights
Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
Revenue increased 100% sequentially to $167.5 million in Q3 2026, compared to $83.8 million in Q2 2026, while representing a more than 16-fold increase from $10.1 million in Q3 2025. On a pro forma organic basis, revenue increased 64% year over year, assuming the businesses owned and operated during Q3 2026 were also owned and operated in Q3 2025. Ondas believes that strong organic growth reflects the benefits of platform scale, shared technology, and expanded customer access. The increase further reflects strong performance across the Company's portfolio, particularly C-UAS systems, where demand remains strong given the long-term need to protect the lower skies across civilian and military airspace, as well as in precision strike and land systems.
Gross profit was $36.5 million in Q3 2026, as compared to $36.1 million in Q2 2026 and $2.6 million in Q3 2025. Gross margin was 21.8% in Q3 2026, as compared to 43.1% in Q2 2026 and 25.8% in Q3 2025. The sequential decline in gross margin was related to higher amortization of capitalized intellectual property, the step-up in acquired inventory associated with purchase accounting, as well as inefficiencies in the early stages of ramping large programs. Adjusted Gross Profit and Adjusted Gross Margin were $58.3 million and 34.8%, respectively, in Q3 2026, as compared to Adjusted Gross Profit and Adjusted Gross Margin of $42.3 million and 50.4%, respectively, in Q2 2026. The increase in Adjusted Gross Profit reflects higher revenue, from organic growth as well as from contributions of businesses acquired during the period. The lower Adjusted Gross Margin percentage reflects production and delivery inefficiencies, particularly in the precision strike segment, which represented a disproportionate share of revenue during the period. The Company expects similar gross margin levels in Q4 2026 due to mix with a recovery to historical levels with normal quarterly variability.
Operating expenses increased to $226.0 million in Q3 2026, compared with $199.1 million in Q2 2026 and $18.1 million in Q3 2025. The increase was primarily driven by $88.1 million of non-cash expenses during the quarter, mainly comprising $57.8 million of stock-based compensation, and $25.3 million of amortization expense, together with $14.1 million of acquisition-related cash expenses. Acquisition-related expenses were elevated due
to the timing of several acquisitions, including DZYNE, which was Ondas' largest acquisition to date.
Adjusted Cash Operating Expenses were $118.7 million in Q3 2026, compared to $88.8 million in Q2 2026 and $10.9 million in Q3 2025. This level of operating expense was consistent with our expectations and reflected the inclusion of acquired businesses during the quarter. The growth in adjusted cash operating expenses reflected the inclusion of newly acquired businesses along with continued investment in Ondas' operating platform and infrastructure in support of our expected significant revenue acceleration in the fourth quarter of 2026 and beyond. Research and development expense increased to $61.6 million in Q3 2026, up $30 million sequentially, reflecting the Company's rapid expansion of internal development capabilities, a significantly accelerated pace of product innovation, and intensified integration efforts across its growing technology platform.
Operating loss increased to $189.5 million in Q3 2026, compared to a $162.9 million loss in Q2 2026, and a $15.5 million loss in Q3 2025. The increase from both periods was the result of the changes described above and includes the aforementioned large non-cash expenses.
Total other income, net was $133.1 million in Q3 2026, compared to other income of $44.2 million in Q2 2026 and other income of $8.3 million in Q3 2025. Other income includes non-cash gains of $125.1 million relating to warrants issued in connection with the October 2025 and January 2026 equity raises. Because these warrants are remeasured at fair value each reporting period, the resulting non-cash gains and losses can create significant volatility in reported earnings that are unrelated to the Company's core operating performance, cash flows, or the economic terms of the warrants.
Net loss was $64.7 million in Q3 2026, which included the non-cash items mentioned above, as compared to net loss of $89.7 million in Q2 2026, and a net loss of $7.5 million in Q3 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $59.7 million in Q3 2026, as compared to a loss of $46.2 million in Q2 2026 and a loss of $8.1 million in Q3 2025. The higher sequential loss reflects the lower sequential gross margin; the investments made in continuing to scale Ondas' operating platform and corporate development activities to support the expected significant revenue expansion in Q4 2026 and into 2027.
A reconciliation of non-GAAP measures including Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Cash Operating Expense, Adjusted Gross Profit and Adjusted Gross Margin, is provided in the attached financial tables.
Operational and Financial Outlook
The Company expects continued strong momentum and is now targeting at least $550 million in full year revenue for 2026, which is an increase from the prior target of between $525 - $550 million. articles.title_orig: Stock futures decline as Huang ouster sends Nvidia reeling, oil prices rise: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Stock futures decline as Huang ouster sends Nvidia reeling, oil prices rise: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Stock futures fell on Thursday as Nvidia shares slumped on the ousting of CEO Jensen Huang and investors' hopes for a resolution in the Middle East soured.
Nasdaq-100 futures lost 1.2%, while S&P 500 futures fell 0.6%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures dropped 47 points, or 0.1%.
Selling pressure on Nvidia resumed in extended U.S. trading after the company announced that Huang has resigned and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. This comes after Huang reportedly had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Shares were down more than 10% following the announcement.
Investors moved into fellow chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom . Both stocks were up around 2%.
However, other key stocks in the AI trade were still down alongside Nvidia. Shares of software company Oracle lost 4%. Neocloud Nebius moved 20% lower in premarket trading Thursday after the company posted better-than-expected third-quarter revenue but offered underwhelming guidance.
On top of the AI pressure, oil prices moved higher after President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post , "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed." U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures rose more than 1% to above $87 per barrel. International benchmark Brent crude futures also advanced more than 1% to above $94.
Energy stocks Chevron and ExxonMobil were roughly 1% higher as well. Meanwhile, healthcare stocks like Eli Lilly gained more than 1%.
The moves come as macro risks are brewing for the market.
"We would be a little circumspect about the bounce-back as there are some things changing at the margin [like] stubborn inflation, more Fed rate hikes, higher long-term interest rates, change in configuration in Washington DC [and] AI/data center regulation demands," said Sameer Samana, head of global equities and real assets at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.
Shares of Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices gained about 3% each in premarket trading after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia.
The company's chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim chief.
Nvidia shares were last down about 10%.
For more, follow along with our live updates of Nvidia and Jensen Huang here .
Initial jobless claims showed a modest pop last week after hovering around their lowest levels since the late 1960s.
First-time filings for unemployment benefits totaled a seasonally adjusted 200,000 for the week ending Nov. 7, a gain of 9,000 from the prior period and higher than the Dow Jones consensus for 195,000, the Labor Department reported Thursday.
Continuing claims, which run a week behind, fell 20,000 to just below 1.7 million.
Nebius shares plummeted in the premarket on Thursday after the neocloud's third-quarter revenue topped analysts' expectations, but its guidance disappointed investors.
The stock was last down almost 16%. That's after it rose more than 15% in Wednesday's regular session.
— Jordan Novet and Sean Conlon
Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang's future as head of one of the most important names in technology hangs in the balance following revelations that he had an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.
Analysts said his ouster could lead to a 20%-plus decline in the shares with the uncertainty that would follow overhanging the stock a bit longer after that.
CNBC Pro subscribers can read more here .
"Jensen Huang is toast," Bill Blain, founder and principal at Wind Shift Capital, said in his morning newsletter. "Nvidia's dependence on Jensen Huang is now exposed as a major market risk. The dominant firm within the AI industry lacks clear succession planning and Huang was seen as the acceptable face of AI by the public."
U.S. Treasury yields were mixed Thursday as bond trading resumed after the Veterans Day closure and investors looked ahead to fresh inflation and housing data for clues about the economy and the Federal Reserve's next move.
The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note — the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — were flat at 4.9920%.
The 2-year Treasury note yield, which is more sensitive to short-term Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, was 3 basis points higher at 4.7568%. The longer-dated 30-year Treasury note yield — which often moves on geopolitical developments — was steady at 5.3403%.
Nvidia shares fell on Thursday as the company's board met to decide whether to remove Jensen Huang as CEO following reports that he had had two extramarital affairs.
Several Wall Street analysts told CNBC that if Huang is removed as CEO, this could lead the stock to fall 20%, given how critical he has been to Nvidia's success. Nvidia's stock is already down more than 20% over the last month.
Shares of Nvidia rivals AMD and Broadcom were up 3.9% and 3%, respectively, in premarket trading. Meanwhile, shares of chip stocks Intel , Marvell , Arm and Qualcomm were all trading lower.
Read the full story here .
Shares listed in Europe edged higher at the open, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 index adding 0.3% shortly after the bell.
Bucking the trend, the regional Stoxx 600 Technology index was down 1.3%. The sector was dragged lower by chip stocks in the wake of speculation Jensen Huang is set to be ousted as Nvidia CEO following news of another extramarital affair.
ASMI was 1.8% lower, ASML shed 3%, Be Semiconductor was down 1.6% and Infineon lost 3.8%.
"In our view the writing is on the wall that Jensen's days at Nvidia could be numbered and we would expect this to be a very fluid situation over the next 48 hours," renowned tech bull Dan Ives said in a note overnight.
"Jensen has created a black eye moment for himself and Nvidia and now has created a spider web of complexity that Wall Street, Silicon Valley, DC, and the global tech ecosystem are trying to figure out what is next."
Ives, who founded Yorkville Ives & Co. earlier this year, was referring to the fallout from reports Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a second affair with an executive at the company, which followed news of an extramarital relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.
"We believe Nvidia's value is $300 per share with Jensen as CEO and $225 per share without Jensen as CEO," Ives said. "The stock will clearly be under pressure with this fluid news but the reality is its a dark day for Nvidia, but the company will navigate this turmoil and get through to the other side and remain a core foundational piece of the AI Revolution."
Rolls-Royce reiterated its full-year profit and cash flow guidance Thursday as demand for power generation equipment used in data centers surged.
Order intake in its power systems business rose 62% in the first nine months of the year, as orders for gas engines nearly tripled year-on-year, driven by power demand from data centers, the company said in a trading update.
The unit's order backlog at the end of September stood at a record £8.6 billion ($11.4 billion).
The British group highlighted strong demand across its power systems, civil aerospace and defense businesses, as it continues to expect underlying operating profit of between £4.7 billion and £4.9 billion in 2026.
In defense, it highlighted progress on military aircraft programmes, including the MQ-25A autonomous refuelling aircraft and the Global Combat Air Programme.
It also said demand remains strong across both widebody and business aviation, as its large engine order backlog grew to around 2,500 engines.
"Given our strong progress this year, we will revisit our mid-term targets at our Full Year results in February," said CEO Tufan Erginbilgic.
It also announced an interim £1.5 billion share buyback as part of an existing program through 2028.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia live updates: Stock tanks after new affair allegations, board reportedly preparing to oust Jensen Huang
articles.title_zh: Nvidia live updates: Stock tanks after new affair allegations, board reportedly preparing to oust Jensen Huang
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to oust chief executive officer Jensen Huang following disclosures regarding two extramarital relationships, including one with a senior corporate subordinate and another involving a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy , as reported by The Wall Street Journal .
The board's impending move follows reporting from The New York Times detailing that Huang maintained an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. The relationship has been discussed inside the company, according to five people who worked at the chip-maker.
Powell, 48, reports directly to the 63-year-old CEO. Both Huang and Powell are married to other people.
According to sources familiar with the matter, Huang and Powell were observed behaving affectionately at a San Jose hotel during Nvidia's GTC developer conference in March.
A bystander recorded the interaction on a smartphone, after which members of Huang's personal security detail sequestered the individual and offered them a non-disclosure agreement to sign, according to three people briefed on the incident. The New York Times noted it had not viewed the video.
During that same conference in March, Powell — who joined Nvidia in 2008 and was promoted to lead its healthcare unit in 2017 — delivered a presentation on artificial intelligence applications in biology that featured cartoon depictions of Huang.
Such relationships conflict directly with Nvidia's corporate code of conduct, which explicitly directs employees to avoid situations, including personal relationships, that generate internal conflicts. The policy states that the company "promptly investigates reports of misconduct."
When reached by phone on Wednesday by The New York Times to address his relationship with Powell, Huang said, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly," before hanging up.
This development compounds an existing crisis surrounding the chip-making giant . Earlier this week, Huang admitted in a memo to Nvidia employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife , following revelations regarding his relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — who U.S. intelligence has said facilitated shipments of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms as part of a foreign intelligence operation. China has denied the espionage claims.
Nvidia's board previously launched an internal investigation into the matter led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Additionally, Republican leaders of three House committees have called for Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing regarding his interactions with the alleged intelligence asset.
The revelations have drawn criticism from lawmakers, investors and Nvidia's board over Huang's conduct.
Nvidia shares fell approximately 8 percent in after-hours trading following Wednesday's reports. The stock has wiped out more than $300 billion in market value since disclosures regarding Alice Huang first emerged.
If Huang leaves, it would create an immediate leadership gap at the $4 trillion chipmaker, which is the driving force behind the global AI boom and the technological rivalry between the U.S. and China.

articles.title_orig: Noctua launches $25 NT-CP1 carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD AM5 and AM4
articles.title_zh: Noctua launches $25 NT-CP1 carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD AM5 and AM4
articles.content_orig:
Noctua says its NT-CP1 thermal pad improves contact through repeated thermal cycles.
A 90 µm thermal pad designed to replace CPU thermal paste.
Noctua has introduced the NT-CP1 AM5/4 carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD Ryzen processors. Developed with Carbice, the pad measures 33 × 33 mm and is 90 µm thick. Its suggested retail price is $24.95 in the US and €24.95 in Europe.
We covered the Noctua and Carbice partnership in June, when the companies planned a September release. The November announcement now provides pricing and final dimensions. The pad supports both AM5 and AM4 processors.
According to Noctua, the NT-CP1 improves thermal contact over the first few hundred to a few thousand thermal cycles. Its carbon nanotubes gradually conform to microscopic surface irregularities. The company says performance then stays stable for years without replacement.
The pad combines carbon nanotubes with an aluminum support layer and a phase-change polymer coating. Installation follows a peel, press and peel process. The slightly tacky coating helps keep the pad in place while mounting the cooler.
Noctua says the coating makes the contact surfaces electrically non-conductive before use, provided the polymer layer is not penetrated. This qualification is relevant when comparing it with other carbon and graphite pads. The announcement focuses on installation and long-term stability rather than quantified temperature gains over thermal paste.
Carbice manufactures the NT-CP1 in the United States using recycled aluminum and waste carbon gas to grow the nanotubes. Noctua says the pad can enter standard aluminum recycling streams. The AM5/4 version has been tuned and validated for AMD Ryzen CPUs and APUs.

articles.title_orig: Nebius falls 10% as company expects increased 2026 capex spend, issues weak outlook
articles.title_zh: Nebius falls 10% as company expects increased 2026 capex spend, issues weak outlook
articles.content_orig:
Nebius shares sank 10% on Thursday as one of the biggest publicly traded neoclouds reported third-quarter revenue that beat analysts' estimates, but issued disappointing guidance.
Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus:
It was not immediately clear if the loss per share was comparable to the 69 cents expected by analysts.
Revenue jumped 571% in the quarter, according to a statement. The company reported a net loss of $37.5 million, a loss of 13 cents per share, compared with $119.6 million, a loss of 50 cents per share, a year earlier.
In a letter to shareholders , CEO Arkady Volozh said the company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue at the low end of the company's $3 billion to 3.4 billion range. FactSet expected full-year revenue of $3.35 billion.
Nebius also shared an initial outlook for 2027, expecting revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, "reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our build-out." FactSet expected 2027 revenue of $12.09 billion.
The company expects FY2026 capital expenditures of $27 billion, higher than its previous capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and the FactSet expectation of $23.85 billion.
Nebius' expected FY2027 capex of $40 billion to $45 billion came in much higher than the FactSet expectation of $28.77 billion.
Nebius' results come after fellow neoclouds CoreWeave and IREN reported better-than-expected financials in their earnings announcements over the past week. That's provided a boost to the companies' stocks, which had suffered steep selloffs in recent weeks on concern about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout.
The neocloud companies posted a robust rally on Wednesday, with Coreweave booming nearly 25%, Nebius climbing 15%, Applied Digital rising more than 7% and IREN adding nearly 6%.
Each of the stocks fell Thursday premarket after the Nebius Q3 report.
Last week, CoreWeave's bond yields spiked past the 16% mark. In its earnings report on Tuesday, CoreWeave told analysts it expects to keep parent-level debt financing under $5 billion through 2027.
The political backdrop has created further volatility as Nebius races rivals to open up new data centers. Last week U.S. voters supported dozens of ballot initiatives to restrict the development of such facilities, while Democrats won sweeping victories in both houses of Congress.
Then there's the Nvidia problem. Following stinging revelations about CEO Jensen Huang's affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, the Wall Street Journal reported late Wednesday that Nvidia's board was planning to push out the company's co-founder.
Nvidia, which has developed the neocloud market by investing in the companies and backstopping some of their projects, held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing .
During the quarter, Nebius said it raised $5.75 billion in debt financing.
Executives will discuss the results with analysts and issue guidance on a conference call starting at 8 a.m. ET.

articles.title_orig: Review: Apple’s M6 iMac is pricey, but it’s still a good choice for a clean desk
articles.title_zh: Review: Apple’s M6 iMac is pricey, but it’s still a good choice for a clean desk
articles.content_orig:
The Apple Silicon iMac got its fourth refresh this month.
Every other Apple Silicon Mac has found a way to move forward over the last half-decade—we’ve gotten a more Pro design for the MacBook Pro, a mini-er design for the Mac mini, and a Mac Studio that has finally made Apple admit it doesn’t want to make the Mac Pro anymore.
But the Apple Silicon iMac has always been more interested in looking backward. It’s the thin, screen-on-a-stand iMac design by way of the original Bondi Blue G3 iMac. It’s a clean and pretty desktop computer, one I see all the time in small offices and on TV shows that depict small offices. We’re long past the days when it was Apple’s primary workstation computer.
So I wanted to write about this new iMac from the perspective of that entry-level iMac buyer, who chooses the iMac because it’s simple and then uses it until it breaks. What does a new iMac get you if you’re stepping up from the M1 model or comparing it against an older refurbished M4 model? Without any real external updates, what makes this iMac iteration interesting?
If you haven’t used an Apple Silicon-era iMac before, here’s a brief primer.
The new iMac is much thinner than the older aluminum Intel models. Its front is mostly one big 24-inch screen, surrounded on all sides by a relatively thick white bezel (I still wish black were at least an option , but Apple apparently doesn’t agree).
White bezel aside, it’s by far Apple’s most colorful computer. The iMacs ship with color-matched fronts, backs, stands, keyboards, mice, trackpads, and cables. Apple has tweaked the color offerings and changed the tints of each specific color a few times over the years, but the M6 iMac uses the same six color tints (plus silver) that the M4 iMac did.
The basic $1,499 iMac is essentially a MacBook Air in terms of ports—it has two Thunderbolt ports on the back and a headphone jack on the left side. Choosing this model also locks you into a lesser version of the Apple M6 with 10 CPU cores and 10 GPU cores instead of 12 of each, a maximum of 24GB of RAM, a minimum of 256GB of storage, and a maximum of 1TB. Its default keyboard doesn’t have Touch ID support, and the only way to get it is to buy the version with the built-in number pad, an $80 upsell.
The $1,699 version is the one to get if you still intend to use the iMac as a workstation. It includes the full-speed version of the M6 with all its CPU and GPU cores intact (though there are performance caveats here we’ll talk about later), plus options for 32GB of RAM and up to 2TB of storage. This version also includes four Thunderbolt ports on the back for connecting additional accessories. Both available keyboards on this version have Touch ID.
A 2.5 gigabit Ethernet port can be added to any iMac for $30. This port is located on the desktop’s power brick rather than the iMac itself, an elegant solution that keeps even a wired Internet connection hidden beneath your desk with the other cables. All iMacs also offer a VESA mount adapter option in place of the default stand at no extra charge.
I still really like the effect created by the color-matched keyboard, mouse/trackpad, and cables—even the white bezel complements the white keycaps and mouse. Just know you’re paying quite a lot for how the desktop looks. The $899 Mac mini is $800 cheaper than the iMac with the same chip, the same amount of RAM, and the same amount of storage. Sure, it would cost something to add a nice-looking 4K monitor, but not $800, even if you go for extra frills like a high refresh rate.
It’s fine that the iMac upcharges you for style and convenience. That’s the point of the computer. Just make sure that’s what you want to pay for.
Here are the basic specs for every entry-level iMac Apple has shipped, going all the way back to the last of the Intel models.
The iMac’s evolution has been slow and gradual during the Apple Silicon era. The computer has never gotten a base storage upgrade, and the base M4 and M6 models still only support a single external display (the upgraded models support two external displays, finally surpassing the old Intel model).
If you have any kind of Apple Silicon iMac and you’re happy with how it’s performing and you’re not hankering for more RAM or more displays, I don’t think the M6 model really adds anything worth upgrading for. It’s definitely faster, but even six years on, the Apple M1 remains perfectly serviceable for daily use, especially when it’s attached to 16GB of RAM.
And if you’re in the market for an iMac now , I think the M4 model still gets you the best bang for your buck if you can find one refurbished or on sale. That one still gets you a minimum of 16GB of RAM, Thunderbolt in all four ports for the four-port model, the 32GB RAM option, the nano-texture display option, and support for multiple external displays (again, in the four-port model).
The M6 iMac builds on that, and it comes with real performance benefits (more on that shortly). But the brightest dividing line in the Apple Silicon iMac model history is between the M3 and M4 model, not the M4 and M6 model. And that’s true despite the two-generation silicon upgrade.
A quick recap on the M6: a total of 12 CPU cores (two super cores, four performance cores, six efficiency cores), either 10 or 12 GPU cores, 16/24/32GB RAM options, and a doubled Neural Engine NPU with 32 cores instead of 16. For the iMac, the M6 also introduces some of the architectural tweaks introduced with the Apple M5, including the addition of neural accelerator hardware to the GPU cores. This boosts the speed of some kinds of local AI workloads compared to the M4, including MetalFX upscaling and frame generation in games.
The M6 in the Mac mini and the M6 in the 14-inch MacBook Pro both perform similarly within a roughly 28 W sustained power envelope. The version with 16GB of RAM will perform slightly worse in games and other workloads sensitive to memory bandwidth—the 16GB M6 offers 153 GB/s of memory bandwidth, and the 24GB and 32GB versions offer 170 GB/s. But that’s a pretty minor difference.
The iMac is slower than either of those two Macs, particularly in multi-core CPU benchmarks and graphics benchmarks, and the HandBrake video encoding test shows the likely culprit. The iMac’s M6 consumes an average of 18 W of power under sustained heavy load. It won’t throttle its speeds as aggressively as a MacBook Air because the iMac still includes an active cooling fan, but the reduced power envelope does mean that the Mac mini or MacBook Pro are 5 to 8 percent faster than the iMac in heavy multi-core CPU tasks and about 8 to 12 percent faster in graphics benchmarks.
One benefit of the smaller power envelope is that the iMac’s chip is even more power-efficient than the regular M6 and the iMac’s version of the M4, using much less power to do the same amount of work.
That still makes it a solid upgrade over the M4. The iMac’s M6 is 15 to 20 percent faster in our single-core CPU benchmarks, between 20 and 30 percent faster in multi-core CPU benchmarks, and between 20 and 40 percent faster in graphics benchmarks (the Blender GPU benchmarks do even better—they seem to like the neural accelerators in the M5 and M6 GPUs). Especially with 24GB or 32GB of RAM, it’s perfectly capable of being the heart of a multi-monitor workstation setup or a light photo/video editing rig.
The M6 iMac changes almost nothing about who the iMac is for, its position in Apple’s lineup, or what it’s technically capable of. It’s a box-ticking upgrade, and the box being ticked is “keep the insides up to date.”
That means today’s iMac is best for the same kinds of computer users it was good for in 1998: people who don’t want a laptop, people who need a friendly and approachable kiosk or office computer, and people who just want something pretty that doesn’t require a lot of fussing with screens or cables.
That’s the main thing I miss about being an iMac user. I like how my current Mac Studio desktop works, and I need flexibilit

articles.title_orig: Two men found guilty of spying for Iran over plan to target journalists
articles.title_zh: Two men found guilty of spying for Iran over plan to target journalists
articles.content_orig:
Two Iranian men have been convicted of spying for an Iranian intelligence service by carrying out surveillance on journalists and a lawyer in the UK.
Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, were convicted of "assisting a foreign intelligence service" at Woolwich Crown Court on Thursday.
They were tasked by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) with monitoring the targets. Sepahvand intended to carry out a "violent attack" against at least one of them, while Manesh helped with planning.
A third man, Shapoor Qalehali Khani Noori, 57, was cleared of the same charge.
Sepahvand was in contact with two men with Iranian telephone numbers.
Police seized 534GB of data that showed Sapahvand and Manesh were given documents that included pictures of targets, their work addresses, the make and colour of their cars and the names of pets. They then used ChatGPT to carry out further research.
The pair, from west London, are asylum seekers who had been granted temporary leave to remain. Sepahvand arrived in the UK in a lorry and Manesh in a small boat.
Sepahvand conducted surveillance and reconnaissance in preparation for inflicting violence on several "subjects" in the UK.
These included journalists Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, who worked for the London-based Persian broadcaster Iran international, Jonathan Turner, a founding member of UK Lawyers for Israel, as well as a media production professional.
Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, the senior national co-ordinator for Counter-Terrorism Policing, said it was the first time ChatGPT case search history had been presented in a state threat case.
She added: "It's something we're beginning to see more of as AI tools become more widely available and people become more aware of them."
It was clear from the evidence at the trial that at times Sepahvand felt he was being mistreated by his Iranian handlers, who had not paid him.
Evans said: "This is a trend we see in these types of cases where people get involved in work on behalf of foreign states and they're often promised money and lots of other things but they rarely receive what they've been offered."
Sepahvand had claimed he participated in the spying out of fear of the consequences of refusing but the prosecution described this as "entirely bogus".
In voice notes sent to an Iranian contact, he said he had been promised that a conviction for theft in Iran would be "sorted out" - which prosecutors said was part of his motivation for conducting the surveillance.
Sepahvand also asked for £150,000 in exchange for "finishing off" a target, stressing that he would "do it".
Frank Ferguson, of the Crown Prosecution Service's counter-terrorism division, said the two men had been promised rewards for sending intelligence back to contacts in Iran.
"Sepahvand himself was willing to go beyond surveillance to commit serious violence against their targets," he said.
"Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place.
"Cases like this show Iranian intelligence's willingness to use proxies to target the regime's critics abroad."
Sepahvand and Manesh will be sentenced at the Old Bailey on 17 December.

articles.title_orig: Boy found alive after 6 days lost in Australian wilderness: "He's grounded for life"
articles.title_zh: Boy found alive after 6 days lost in Australian wilderness: "He's grounded for life"
articles.content_orig:
A 17-year-old boy with autism was found alive Thursday after six days lost in eastern Australian woodlands.
The boy, whom police identified only as William, had begun camping with a teenage friend when he disappeared last Friday near Walhalla, a former gold-mining town 185 kilometers (115 miles) east of Melbourne, police said.
A police helicopter crew found him surrounded by wilderness lying asleep on a flat rock beside a creek, and he was later reunited with his mother. William was in good spirits and mostly in good health, the police statement said.
Video shot from the rescue helicopter showed he was shirtless and sunburned. He was wearing shorts and boots and was using towels as blankets.
"I'm just over the moon that he's alive," his mother, Elizabeth, told reporters. The AP has decided not to provide her family name to avoid identifying her son.
"And he's never leaving the house again. He's grounded for life. He's not going anywhere ever again," she joked.
Police video showed Elizabeth embrace her son after the rescue helicopter landed to complete its mission.
William was later taken to a hospital for his health to be monitored, police said.
"Amazingly, William is in good spirits and for the most part, in good health," they said in the statement.
William's family have said he has Level 2 autism. That requires "substantial support," according to the Australian advocacy group Autism360.
Such a person may have marked deficits in verbal and non-verbal social communication and rely heavily on routines and predictable activities. Disruption can cause significant distress.
The Southern Hemisphere spring weather had been mild for the past week in the alpine region where William was lost and there had been little rain.
Elizabeth had dropped off her son and his friend last Friday for a weekend of camping. William walked a short distance from the campsite to the drop-off location to collect more camping equipment but never returned to his friend, police said.
After becoming lost, William trekked for days up and down "some very steep terrain," Acting Police Inspector Jason Benbow said.
He spent the last two days where he was found at the creek, trapped by the steepness of his surrounds 2 kilometers (1.2 miles) from the his camp site, Benbow said.
"He woke up to the sound of the helicopter, gave them a thumbs up and they winched him to safety," Benbow told reporters.
The extensive police search for him involved more than 100 emergency services personnel and volunteers.
There have been other dramatic rescues in Australia's wilderness in recent years.
In 2025, a German tourist was found alive in Australia's remote Outback, 12 days after she went missing. She was found just a day after officials and local media said an Australian surfer , who had been feared lost at sea, was rescued after spending a night on an uninhabited island miles from where they had walked into the water.
In 2019, an Australian woman missing for three days was rescued after the SOS message she scrawled in the sand was spotted on a surveillance camera.
The successful rescues have included animals as well. Last year, a runaway dog was captured after a 529-day adventure in Australia as she roamed an island teeming with kangaroos, possums, koala bears and penguins.
Agence  France-Presse contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: COP31: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'
articles.title_zh: COP31: Burnham says climate consensus 'gone' but pledges 'new era of leadership'
articles.content_orig:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has warned that the consensus on both science and climate change has "gone".
Addressing other world leaders and delegates at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey, he said that despite this, the UK was ready to begin a "new era of British leadership" on the climate change issue.
But environmental campaigners at the summit said the PM had to back up his warm words with stronger actions.
In recent months, the UK government has announced policies which critics say have weakened its green credentials, such as reducing support for heat pumps, approving the Jackdaw gas field and doubling down on support for Heathrow Airport's expansion.
Burnham opened his speech on Thursday by talking about the heat experienced in the UK this past summer.
He said "it was not normal" - in fact it was the hottest on record, made 130 times more likely because of climate change, according to the Met Office .
Hundreds of schools were closed, cereal harvests were down 11%, and ambulance services were inundated with calls beyond levels seen during the Covid-19 pandemic.
As a result of the threat to people's health and homes, the PM said he was creating the UK, and the world's, first climate security envoy, Dame Madeleine Alessandri.
Alessandri, the former head of the Joint Intelligence Committee, said: "Climate change and nature loss are increasingly shaping the security environment in which the UK operates."
As a result this was "placing additional pressure on resources, economies and communities around the world", she added.
This will be seen as a strong indication of the focus of the UK's priorities when it takes up the G20 presidency next year.
The current president is the US, which has been a notable absentee from the COP process over the last two years since President Trump withdrew the country from the most important global climate treaty - the Paris Climate Agreement.
Professor Lord Nicholas Stern, who identified 20 years ago that climate change could cost the global economy up to 20% of GDP if left unchecked, praised the PM's words.
"The Prime Minister was right to identify climate change as a threat to security around the world, and the importance of investments in clean electricity generation as the best way of protecting households and businesses from the high prices and volatile markets for fossil fuels," he said.
On tackling the causes of climate change, Burnham said his government remained committed to meeting the country's target of net zero by 2050 whilst also getting bills down.
He said key to this was cutting our "dependence on fossil fuels" and increasing electrification - the amount of our energy needs met from renewable electricity.
The main driver of rising global temperatures has been the increasing concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, largely caused by burning fossil fuels.
Turkey, the co-hosts of COP31, wants a key outcomes of this year's summit to be a commitment by countries to meet 35% of their energy supply from electricity by 2035. Currently, it is around a fifth.
But Burnham has been accused of having double standards.
"The Prime Minister simply cannot call for clean power across the world while saying yes to more fossil fuels in the UK," said Beth John, climate adviser at Oxfam.
Last month, the government approved the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea on the grounds that it provided energy security.
And in the budget last month Chancellor John Healey announced a funding cut to the Warm Homes Plan, which provides grants and loans to support the installation of heat pumps.
Whilst this week there has been media speculation that the government is considering watering down electric car sales targets, although the government insists no decision has been made.
Successfully switching petrol and diesel cars to EVs and moving from gas boilers to electric-powered heat pumps are key ways to achieve the 35% electrification target .
Although there was no royal presence this year, King Charles III sent a message ahead of Burnham's speech.
"As the world gathers for Cop31, I can only hope that this same spirit of partnership and common purpose can help inspire the collective action that our planet – and future generations – so urgently need.
"Our children and grandchildren will not judge us by the promises we made, but by what we chose to do."
Burnham was the only G7 leader to speak at this year's conference in a sign of faltering support for the COP process - something he acknowledged in his speech.
In an almost word for word copy of Sir Keir Starmer's address last year he said: "The consensus we once enjoyed on science and climate has gone, and the reality is now the world will reach 1.5 degrees."
Other leaders expected to speak on Thursday include many island states like Tonga, Tuvalu and the Solomon Islands.
For these nations, the impact of climate change is already at their front door. With most of their land just metres above sea level, rising water levels have caused many to abandon their homes in recent years.
Last year, Australia - the co-host of the COP31 summit - opened up the world's first climate visa for Tuvalu citizens wanting to evacuate.
The first intake was massively oversubscribed, with more than a third of the population entering the ballot.
As glaciers continue to melt and oceans expand, average sea levels are expected to keep climbing and potentially accelerate. The World Meteorological Organisation said on the opening day of this conference the global mean sea level was at its highest level since records began.

articles.title_orig: China’s diaspora crackdown reaches deep into Europe, report finds
articles.title_zh: China’s diaspora crackdown reaches deep into Europe, report finds
articles.content_orig:
THE HAGUE — Beijing is overseeing nearly 1,250 overseas policing outposts in more than 90 countries to crack down on dissidents, according to a report by a human rights advocacy organization.
The report described Europe as a hotspot with hundreds of Beijing’s policing offices across some two dozen European countries, which it said exposed China’s growing attempts to control its diaspora.
Researchers at the Spain-based organization, Safeguard Defenders, gathered open-source evidence from the Chinese Party-state to examine the extent to which the Chinese diaspora is monitored, surveilled and policed around the world.
These policing outposts “act as the Chinese Communist Party operatives for community surveillance and enforcement abroad,” according to the report.
The report lands at an awkward time for Europe’s trade officials. Ditte Juul Jørgensen, head of the EU’s trade department — which has been working to balance the trade relationship with Beijing — will meet with China’s Vice Minister of Commerce Ling Ji in Brussels on Thursday.
Europe is attempting to walk a fine line with its relations with Beijing. EU legislation proposed in January seeks to kick risky Chinese suppliers out of Europe’s most critical industries over cybersecurity concerns, while supply chain dependencies and political coercion remain ongoing challenges. The EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas has also raised concerns about what she said was China’s enabling of Russia’s war in Ukraine and credible reports of China training Russia’s military .
The report builds on initial revelations from Safeguard Defenders in 2022 that identified more than 100 facilities around the world, which the NGO described as overseas outposts of China’s security apparatus. Back then, that report said Beijing announced its “first batch” of “30 overseas police service stations in 25 cities in 21 countries.”
Following the revelations, some governments denounced the overseas police stations as illegal, and some pursued criminal investigations, the NGO said in its latest report. In response, Beijing claimed the stations had been closed, it added.
“Far from closing, the evidence shows expansion: today more than 10 police forces from five Chinese provinces work through a global network of Chinese Communist Party operatives abroad,” the new report says.
The latest paper was presented at a conference hosted by the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (IPAC), a gathering of 52 cross-party lawmakers from 30 countries that campaigns for a more coordinated response to the Chinese Communist Party. Policymakers raised numerous concerns at the event in The Hague earlier this month — about what they considered security threats of critical infrastructure, trade dependencies and potential risks from a future conflict between China and Taiwan that would disrupt shipping.
The Chinese foreign ministry and state media have previously called IPAC an “anti-China” group and accused it of spreading disinformation and interfering in China’s internal affairs, particularly over Taiwan.
China’s Ministry for Foreign Affairs and its European Union mission didn’t respond to requests for comment on the report. China has previously denied running overseas police stations and says it doesn’t interfere in other countries’ internal affairs and that it respects international law.
In 2023, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson rejected the term “police stations,” saying the “institutions helped overseas Chinese who could not return to China due to the pandemic, renew their driving licence and perform physical examination.”
These 1,250 offices were “the tip of the iceberg,” according to the NGO, which said it was conservative in how it mapped and linked them to China’s policing system. To be counted, they had to be officially connected to China’s police or prosecutors and have open-source evidence of overseas activities, report author Laura Harth said. This meant broader influence or interference operations were excluded.
“All of them serve to control and instill fear in diaspora communities … all of them represent a standing national security risk,” she said.
Slovakian MEP Miriam Lexmann, who is part of the European Parliament’s trade committee and China delegation — lawmakers tasked with maintaining and managing legislative ties between the EU and China — said people needed to become more aware of the security threats posed by China.
“It means that our free countries are no longer free anymore for everyone because they are not able to guarantee freedom of speech, freedom of behavior to people who are in our country,” she told POLITICO in reference to the operations.
China’s surveillance through facial recognition and interference in communications was “the exact behavior of the former Soviet Stasi,” she said, but worse since the technology is now much more sophisticated.
The main concern expressed by lawmakers attending the IPAC conference was China’s relationship with Russia, and its help in propping up the Kremlin’s war in Ukraine. Their discussions included what this could mean for a future conflict and war on two fronts if Beijing were to try and take Taiwan militarily while NATO countries were attacked by Russia.
“The road to escalation in the Taiwan Strait can run right through what’s happening in Ukraine and in Kyiv,” said Dutch lawmaker Jan Paternotte, who co-chaired the IPAC conference.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft confirms Windows security updates installation issues
articles.title_zh: Microsoft confirms Windows security updates installation issues
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft has confirmed reports that the November 2026 security updates are failing to install on Windows 11 systems with the October preview update.
This follows widespread reports that the KB5132061 update fails to install , with affected users seeing the installation process lock midway and then trigger 0x800f0989 or 0x800f0993 errors.
"When attempting to install the November 2026 Windows security update (the Originating KBs listed above), some devices might be unable to complete the installation. Affected devices might repeatedly attempt to install the update or display error code 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, or 0x800f0993," Microsoft said in a service update seen by BleepingComputer.
"This issue affects a limited number of devices that installed the October 2026 non-security preview update (KB5127936). Devices that did not install the October 2026 non-security preview update are not affected."
Microsoft also told IT administrators that the installation issues will resolve automatically for all affected customers by Friday morning and that end users do not need to take any action to receive the fix.
"All affected devices should be repaired in 24 to 48 hours starting from November 11, 2026, 10am PT. Once your device receives the repair, it will automatically download and install the November 2026 security update via Windows Update," it added.
The company also urged admins still receiving reports of installation issues after 48 hours to contact Microsoft Support.
This is not the first time Microsoft has had to address Windows update installation issues since the start of the year. In March, it had to pull a buggy Windows 11 non-security preview update (KB5079391) because of 0x80073712 errors during installation.
In May, it also fixed installation failures and 0x800f0922 errors when deploying the May 2026 Windows 11 security update ( KB5089549 ).
More recently, in June, Microsoft warned users that they may encounter issues installing the latest monthly updates and see 0x80073712 or 0x800f0993 errors on some Windows devices upgraded to Windows 11 24H2 or 25H2.

articles.title_orig: US envoys arrive in Moscow for Ukraine talks with Vladimir Putin
articles.title_zh: US envoys arrive in Moscow for Ukraine talks with Vladimir Putin
articles.content_orig:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said his country's military was again facing "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade service, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.
Starshield is owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX company and plays a vital role in military operations.
Ukraine was "trying to clear up all circumstances with the American side", Zelensky said.
His comments come as US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, a day after the latest talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine wrapped up in Abu Dhabi.
Kushner and Witkoff are then expected to travel to Dublin, where they will meet Zelensky.
A similar issue with Starshield connectivity affected the front line in late October and lasted about a week before it was fixed. It remained unclear who ordered the temporary restrictions on Starshield services, with US officials and SpaceX offering differing explanations.
Zelensky said the current disruption had been ongoing for several days and was "helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine".
Videos shared by Russian media on Thursday showed Kushner and Witkoff disembarking a plane and being welcomed by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev with handshakes and hugs.
On Tuesday, Kushner said the US had seen "some openings and some opportunities" and that they would try to "make some progress" at the meeting with Putin.
The in-person talks with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents were only announced on Wednesday after two days of talks which were framed as centred around the postwar security architecture of Europe.
Nearly five years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Moscow shows no sign of backing down from its maximalist demands for sovereign Ukrainian territory and for Western countries to give up any future commitment to protecting Kyiv in case of further attacks.
During the first years of the war, Europeans cut communications with the Kremlin and refused to engage with Russia directly.
However, in recent times many have grown concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin, and have been pushing for a seat at the negotiating table.
The talks in Abu Dhabi were led by the Americans and only included Russia and Ukraine, but Kushner said he and Witkoff would ask Putin to "give his blessing" to invite European representatives in future discussions - particularly with regards to the future configuration of their continent's security architecture.
Kushner also urged Europe to "identify one person to speak on their behalf" in the negotiations.
But the Russians have been opposed to the idea, citing Europe's support for Kyiv as an obstacle.
Vladimir Medinsky, who headed the Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi, said he thought all parties had "moved closer to achieving peace" but that now "a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the United States, and on whether Europe comes to its senses".

articles.title_orig: Scoop: Lutnick stalled curbing Nvidia chip sales to China — again — after Oval Office showdown
articles.title_zh: Scoop: Lutnick stalled curbing Nvidia chip sales to China — again — after Oval Office showdown
articles.content_orig:
Published: November 12, 2026 at 7:09a.m. EST
WASHINGTON -- U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick stalled President Donald Trump’s crackdown on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia’s chips to China, Axios reported on Wednesday, citing high-level sources.
Trump on Thursday of last week authorized a crackdown on companies suspected of diverting the chips for the third time this year, Axios reported, adding that the Republican president consulted billionaire Elon Musk before giving the go-ahead.
But Axios reported that Lutnick has repeatedly stood in the way.
The White House and a spokesperson for Lutnick did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Lutnick met in the Situation Room last Thursday with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Axios said.
During the meeting, Bessent confronted Lutnick about resistance from his department to implementing export controls. Lutnick appeared to agree but said he needed to check with Trump, according to the Axios report.
Several U.S. lawmakers have said in recent days they want the Trump administration to take a tougher stance on exporting U.S. chips to China and have called on Congress to approve legislation toughening restrictions, following disclosures about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Nvidia’s board launched ​an investigation after reports that Huang ⁠had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman ​who U.S. intelligence officials believed was spying for Beijing.
In June, Reuters reported that the Trump administration had held off from adding China’s AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks to a trade blacklist.
The U.S. has not posted any additions to its Entity List since October 2025, the longest stretch between new postings in ‌more than a ⁠decade.
